chapter_theme: The close of the woman's lament: the Lord set his feet in her stone heart, burned her bonds with a look and told her to stay, showed her his form of consciousness and swallowed her as ghee is held in milk; the ages of dying and being born in hell are nothing now, karma and the four wombs have lost their name, and he who is beyond the three voids and beyond simile has come to earth as the guru. The work ends by asking the knowers of the three voids to forgive similes that fail.
structure_note: Still in the woman's voice (அடி, ஆண்டி, காண்). 607 to 614 are what he did and said to her; 615 to 620 are her account of her own state, with the first-person ஆனேன் and அறிந்தேன் replacing the refrain; 621 is a blessing on the guru's feet and 622 the poet's apology for his comparisons, closing the work.

607.reading: As if a blue lily had bloomed inside a heart of stone, he set his twin feet inside my heart.
607.nuance: The stone heart is hers, the flower his doing; grace is pictured as the impossible bloom, not as her own softening.

608.reading: He is the horse of the Vedas, yet those who gallop on it do not know him; he is knowledge that no ear brings, and only those with the right intent see it.
608.nuance: காதற்ற ஞானம் can be 'earless knowledge', knowledge not gained by hearing (கேள்வி), or 'knowledge without edge or handle', unbounded. The Veda-horse image, ridden fast and getting nowhere, favours the first: reciting is not knowing.

609.reading: With a look that saw through the deeds of bondage, he showed me love and said: stay.
609.nuance: The printed பட்ப்பார்த்த is corrupt; பட்டப் பார்த்த (looked so that they were struck) or படப் பார்த்த (looked so that they perished) both give a gaze that undoes bondage. நில் (stand, stay) is the one word he speaks.

610.reading: The place where sound subsides is the light within Om; this, he said, is the Brahman that stays without speaking.
610.nuance: The silent Brahman of 598 and 606 is here located: at the end of sound, inside the syllable. Light is found where sound ends, as in the Siddhars' nada-ending teaching.

611.reading: With the good gaze of consciousness he showed me the form of pure consciousness, made me of his own nature and stood there as himself.
611.nuance: நோக்கு, the gaze, is one of the traditional modes of the guru's initiation (looking, touching, thinking); here the look alone transforms. தன்மயம் ஆக்கி, 'made me of his nature', is union without loss of him.

612.reading: He himself looked at me, and now there is nothing but himself; what can I say, girl? There is no place left from which to tell it.
612.nuance: நவில இடம் இல்லை repeats 603; after union there is no standpoint for a speaker, which the next verses and 622 nevertheless go on speaking from.

613.reading: To all the people who are here today and die tomorrow he said: stay sweetly forever in the all-fullness.
613.nuance: The remedy for mortality is not another life but dwelling in the Fullness; the verse addresses everyone, not only the speaker.

614.reading: Is it not easy if you only look? Is it not the attachment-free attachment? He came to this earth to show the place to everyone.
614.nuance: பற்றற்ற பற்று, attachment to the one without attachment, is the Kural's paradox at 350; இடம் காட்ட is to show the place or way, the guru's office.

615.reading: All this time of dying and being born, girl: none of it is anything now; I have become water on iron.
615.nuance: இரும்பில் உறை நீர் is water that falls on hot iron and vanishes without trace, as 620 makes explicit with தீயிரும்பு; the past births are gone as if they never were.

616.reading: In what age did it all happen, the dying and being born? All that time I lay sunk in a hell.
616.nuance: Hell is not a place after death but the whole span of rebirth seen from the far side of it. ஆநரகில் may be அந்நரகில், that hell.

617.reading: Time has passed away, all karma has gone, and the four kinds of womb have lost even their name.
617.nuance: The four births of tradition are from egg, sweat, sprout and womb (அண்டசம், சுவேதசம், உற்பீசம், சராயுசம்); நாம நட்டம், loss of name, is the same phrase 603 used of the Lord, now used of the wombs.

618.reading: Beyond the three voids, as the first void and the whole First, he has come just now and swallowed me up.
618.nuance: முப்பாழ், the three voids, is Tirumular's scheme (the voids of maya, of knowledge and of calm, or of soul, Supreme and union); Pattinathar sets the Lord beyond even these as முதற்பாழ், the first void. விழுங்கிக் கொண்டான், 'he swallowed me', is the work's word for union (619).

619.reading: As ghee is held in milk, the supreme light embraced me and swallowed me wholly.
619.nuance: Ghee in milk is the stock Saiva image of the Lord present unseen in the soul; here it is turned around, the soul being taken into the light.

620.reading: I became a painted picture, water on red-hot iron; and I knew the awareness that calls the state where all is level 'sleep'.
620.nuance: தெத்தபடம் is obscure (perhaps தத்தப்படம், a picture or screen, a mere image); the iron image repeats 615. ஒத்த இடம் நித்திரை may mean that the state of evenness beyond waking and dream is what the traditions call sleep, or that for her it is indistinguishable from sleep; the line turns on technical words of the avastha scheme.

621.reading: Long live the feet of him who came to this earth as the guru: the substance without equal or simile, hard to put into words.
621.nuance: The work's many similes (ch. 34) are here disowned in advance: he is ஒப்பும் உவமையும் அற்ற, beyond likeness. What is reachable is the guru on earth, named in 614 as the one who came to show the place.

622.reading: Though I have spoken comparisons and though my similes have gone wrong, the elders who have learned and realised the three voids will bear with me and grant grace.
622.nuance: ஒப்பாரி is both a comparison and a funeral lament, which is what a புலம்பல் is; the poet apologises for both. The judges he names are not the Lord but those who know the three voids, the knowers of the Tirumanthiram's scheme.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar's Lord enters his heart and makes it his temple, as the water is held in the coconut; Pattinathar's sets his feet in a heart of stone as a lily blooms in it. Both make the heart the shrine, and in both it is the Lord who enters, not the devotee who builds.

Sivavakkiyar: recite the Sama and the four Vedas and you still do not know Siva; Pattinathar: ride the Veda-horse at a gallop and you do not know him. Both place knowing after reciting and locate it within intent, not text.
Both end speech at the Supreme: Tirumular's pure form beyond the three voids is where words come to their end, Pattinathar's silent Brahman is the light at the place where sound subsides within Om.

Sivavakkiyar asks what he can say of what has no grammar, there being nothing within him but the Lord and I; Pattinathar, looked at by the Lord, finds nothing but him and no place to speak from. Both make the end of the self the end of saying.

The Kural says cling to the clinging of the one who has no clinging, so as to let clinging go; Pattinathar names the same thing பற்றற்ற பற்று and adds that the Lord came to earth to show it. The Kural's paradox is made a person.

Tirumular names the three voids, of maya, of space and of the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti; Pattinathar takes the scheme as known and places the Lord beyond it as a first void and whole First that comes and swallows the soul.

Sivavakkiyar's sinners do not know the Lord who is in them like ghee hidden in milk; Pattinathar's supreme light holds and swallows him as milk holds ghee. One uses the image for the unseen presence, the other for accomplished union.

Tirumular says that beyond the light in the void there is nothing here to compare it with; Pattinathar's guru is the substance without equal or simile. Both put the Supreme past comparison, and Pattinathar then apologises (622) for having compared.

Tirumular's experience is in the three voids where words cease; Pattinathar names those who have learned and realised the three voids as the judges of his failed words. The three voids are the point where both poets expect speech to break down.

source_issues: 607 line 2 is printed என்னென்சினுள்ளே for என்னெஞ்சினுள்ளே.
609 line 1 பட்ப்பார்த்த is corrupt: a bare ப் stands where a vowel sign is missing (பட்டப் or படப்).
The units of this work are printed without word-spacing; 620 line 1 (தெத்தபடமானேண்டி) cannot be divided with confidence.
